chunk_findings.detail: `core.fuzzy.ratio` / `available` are no longer the adapter functions that read `DEFAULT` at call time. Previously `adapters.fuzzy.ratio` did `return DEFAULT.ratio(a, b)` and core re-exported that object, so `ddflow.adapters.fuzzy.DEFAULT = FakeFuzzy()` (the stand-in the module itself documents) made `from ddflow.core.fuzzy import ratio; ratio("x", "yyyy")` return the fake score. After this change core binds its own `_fuzz` once via `from ..adapters.fuzzy import _fuzz` and calls `_likeness` directly, so the same input returns the real rapidfuzz/difflib score and ignores the replaced `DEFAULT`. `from ddflow.adapters.fuzzy import ratio` now raises `ImportError` because those names were removed from the adapter `__all__` and module body. That is a caller-visible behaviour change, not a pure re-export.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/fuzzy.py:29

chunk_findings.detail: `from ..adapters.fuzzy import _fuzz` copies the name; it does not keep one binding. After `import ddflow.adapters.fuzzy as af` and `import ddflow.core.fuzzy as cf`, `af._fuzz = None` makes `af.DEFAULT.available()` False while `cf.available()` stays True and `cf.ratio("Hello", "hello")` still uses rapidfuzz. Previously `core.fuzzy.available`/`ratio` were the adapter functions, so they read `adapters.fuzzy._fuzz` and `DEFAULT`. The same split applies to `cc_visit` re-bound in `ddflow/services/complexity_budget.py`: patching `adapters.complexity.cc_visit` no longer changes `complexities()` there, so the two homes can disagree about whether the extra is installed.
